summary: Defines a subcode for the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message to be used when a BGP session is closed because of a BFD session going down. This helps operators see the real reason a connection ended.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9384 defines a BGP Cease subcode named BFD Down for connections closed after a BFD session goes down. The code helps the neighbor identify the reason when the notification can be delivered.

questions: why did my bgp session go down
what is the bgp bfd down subcode
subtitle: A BGP notification subcode that identifies a BFD-down session closure.

tldr.problem: When a BGP connection closes because BFD detected a loss of connectivity, the neighbor may not know why the session ended.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC allocates the BFD Down subcode under the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION code and recommends sending it when possible.
tldr.outcome: Operators can distinguish BFD-detected failure from other BGP issues, while a complete loss of connectivity may prevent the notification from arriving.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 9384's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines a BGP Cease notification subcode for BFD-triggered session closure.

sections.title: Why Label a BFD-Triggered Closure
sections.content:
BFD detects loss of connectivity between forwarding engines, often faster than the timers used by a routing protocol. BGP can use BFD to close a session more quickly when the BFD session changes to Down.

This RFC defines a Cease NOTIFICATION subcode that identifies this specific reason for closing a BGP connection. It helps the other speaker and network operators correlate the closure with a BFD event.
sections.plainLanguage: BFD can detect a connection problem before BGP's own timers do. A specific notification code tells the neighbor that BFD triggered the BGP shutdown.

sections.title: Sending the BFD Down Subcode
sections.content:
IANA assigned value 10 to the BFD Down subcode in the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION registry. When a BGP connection is terminated because a BFD session goes Down, the speaker should send a NOTIFICATION with error code Cease and subcode BFD Down.

If the connectivity loss is total, the notification may not be deliverable. The RFC recommends that speakers still record the reason in their operational state.
sections.plainLanguage: The speaker sends BFD Down as the reason for a BFD-triggered session closure when it can. If the link is completely unavailable, it should still record the reason locally.

sections.title: Partial and Total Connectivity Loss
sections.content:
A BFD session may go down during only a partial loss of connectivity. In that case, the remote BGP speaker may still receive the Cease NOTIFICATION and learn that BFD detected a problem rather than the BGP speaker itself having an issue.

Operators choose BFD timers based on factors such as stability and speed of failure detection. If a Hard Reset subcode is required, the BFD Down reason should be carried in the notification's data portion as described by the RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: A notification can explain a BFD failure even if some traffic still passes. Operators balance fast detection against the stability of their chosen BFD timers.
